Checking for a system text-to-speech engine…
Automatic uses the phone\'s text-to-speech engine.
No system text-to-speech engine is set, so Automatic uses the built-in voice. On GrapheneOS, pick Speech Services as the preferred engine to use it.
Used when the engine is Built-in, or when no system engine is set.
Short leaves the distance off the prompt at the turn itself.
Even while the voice speaks, for bikes and loud cars.
Road alerts from the map data
Flock and other ALPR cameras mapped in OpenStreetMap. Checked on the phone; nothing about your drive is sent.

Southbound keeps maps, search, routing and voice on your phone. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), shown with the OpenMapTiles schema (© OpenMapTiles). Routing by Valhalla; navigation by Ferrostar (Stadia Maps); map rendering by MapLibre. Built-in voice: Piper \"Amy\" (Mycroft mimic3-voices) run by sherpa-onnx.
Everything above works offline. These extras go online only when turned on, and fetch whole feeds, so nothing sent says where you are, what you searched or where you\'re going.
Arrival times and service alerts from MTA. No key needed.
Needs a free key from bustime.mta.info. Stored encrypted on this phone.
Bus Time key saved (type to replace)
Crashes, closures and work zones across the state, fetched whole every few minutes. Routes steer around closures. Needs a free developer key from 511ny.org.
Speeds on NYC highways and main roads from NYC Open Data, fetched whole. No key needed. The city\'s copy sometimes lags; readings older than two hours are not shown.
With either on, a traffic button appears on the map. Feeds are fetched only while the layer is shown or while navigating.
Version %1$s is ready. Confirm the install when Android asks.

Maps for the regions below, statewide search and directions, and NYC transit data from Southbound\'s GitHub releases, checked daily. Only the files that changed are downloaded, and each is checked against its published SHA-256.
New versions of Southbound from the same releases, checked to be signed with the same key. Android asks you to confirm the first one; after that Southbound updates itself.
Off: downloads wait for Wi-Fi. Check now always downloads straight away.

The repository is private, so GitHub needs a token: a fine-grained personal access token with read-only Contents access to StrongHorse44/maps. It\'s stored encrypted on this phone and sent only to api.github.com.
Queued: Android starts it once there\'s a connection (Wi-Fi, unless mobile data is allowed). If this stays for more than a minute, close and reopen Southbound.
Tick the parts of New York you want maps for. Search and directions cover the whole state in one download each; transit schedules cover NYC. Unticking a region deletes its map from the phone.
Not downloaded yet; comes with the next update check.
